title: Cold, mottled, bluish, or patchy skin near death

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources provide broad family-facing descriptions; clinical review is needed before public rendering.
Skin changes vary by body, lighting, illness, and skin tone; this pilot is not yet adequate for equity-sensitive description.

moment.plain_scene: A person near death may have cooler limbs or skin that appears bluish, mottled, patchy, uneven, or bruised-looking in some places.

content_layers.observation_text: Public family-facing and consumer medical sources describe cool limbs and bluish, mottled, or patchy skin among possible physical signs near death.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Hospice UK frames these changes as related to reduced circulation and body slowing; Merck lists cool, bluish, or mottled limbs among characteristic physical signs that death is near.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record exposes a design debt: many public descriptions assume visual access on lighter skin or use color words without enough skin-tone nuance. Future records need careful multisource and practitioner review on how mottling and pallor are perceived across bodies.

what_this_is_not: not a diagnosis of a vascular problem
not universally visible in the same way on all skin tones
not a reason to massage or reposition without care-team guidance
uncertainties: Public sources rarely describe these changes across skin tones well.
Lighting, bedding, room temperature, and illness can change what witnesses perceive.
The record needs bedside-worker language and family accounts.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should name coldness and mottling plainly, avoid graphicness, and encourage contacting the care team when changes worry the family.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect better skin-tone-aware language and how workers explain reduced circulation without overclaiming timing.
language_notes: Ordinary-language search phrases are retained as search aliases, not as diagnostic labels.
Professional terms are index handles; they do not collapse all contexts into one cause or one meaning.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the v2 witnessed-moment schema. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical safety review and ensure lay surface directs urgent or worried readers to qualified local support.
